Subject: Safeguard handback and signed deletion attestation request

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

We're kicking off a SOC 2 sub-process for a scoped customer audit and need to close the loop on a tenant-scoped log disposal that was executed last quarter for our environment "MedShore Prod". The auditor asked us to obtain a signed deletion attestation from Redwood that covers:

- Exact datasets removed (debug traces / session logs / ephemeral caches)
- Preservation snapshot metadata (hashes, time window, custodian manifest) retained for 90 days in case of forensic follow-up
- Confirmation that raw customer prompt/response content was either redacted or excluded from the snapshot

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) provide a DocuSign-ready attestation, 2) produce a preservational manifest (not the raw logs) and 3) confirm the retention window for the manifest?

We are aiming to close this item with the auditor within 10 business days. Please advise timeline and any data samples you can share for internal review.

Thanks,
Lily Turner
Director, Compliance & Risk
MedShore Health

Hi Lily —

Thanks for the clear asks. We can support this request. High-level plan:

1) Attestation: We'll prepare a redwood-signed deletion attestation (DocuSign link) that enumerates the scoped artifacts removed and cites the internal retention policy applied. I attached our attestation template for your review.

2) Preservation manifest: We'll produce a manifest that contains non-sensitive metadata only (timestamps, SHA256 hashes of archived files, scope window, operator id). No raw prompt/response data will be included by default.

3) Retention window: Redwood can retain the manifest and associated custody record for 90 days post-request (we can extend by agreement).

Proposed timeline: initial artifacts and the DocuSign envelope prepared in 5 business days; final signed attestation within 10 business days depending on your review cycle. If you need acceleration, let us know and we can prioritize.

I've looped in Priyom from Legal for any language changes and Kimberly from Security to confirm redaction approach.

Attaching: deletion-attestation-template.pdf (editable).

Regards,

Thank you Karthik — that timeline looks reasonable. One follow-up: the auditor is specifically asking whether the preservation snapshot could contain unredacted prompt/response pairs if an operator had escalated and included them in a trace. Can you confirm the default snapshot composition and whether raw conversational content would ever be present in the preserved metadata bundle?

If raw content can appear in any case, we'll need explicit language in the attestation and an option for a redacted-only manifest.

Also: is Redwood able to sign the attestation on company letterhead and provide a custodian manifest listing the operator IDs that performed the disposal?

Best,
Lily
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>

Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Safeguard handback and signed deletion attestation request

Hi Lily —

Short answer: default preserved bundles do NOT include unredacted prompt/response content. We retain minimal forensic metadata unless a specific escalation requires full-session capture (and in that scenario audit controls + customer consent are required).

Clarifications:
- Default manifest fields we will provide: file hash (SHA256), creation timestamp, scope window, operator id (pseudonymized id), retention expiry.
- Redaction: if a preserved trace originally contained PII, our pipeline applies an automated redaction pass. If a manual snapshot was taken during an incident and contains raw content, that snapshot is treated as an incident artifact and is only captured with explicit customer authorization and logged in our incident ticket.
- Yes, we can provide the attestation on Redwood letterhead and include a custodian manifest that lists operator IDs (pseudonymized by default) plus a reference to the incident/ticket ID if one exists.

I'm attaching a sample forensic-snapshot-sample.json and a short redaction-protocol-summary.pdf so you can review the fields and formatting.

- Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
